Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO. -W S. IUL 05 2024 MARIA LOURDES L. AGUSTIN, CESO Ill Regional Director DILG-National Capital Region 4th Floor, Annex Building — SRA, Sugar Center Compound, North Avenue, Diliman, Quezon City Dear RD Agustin: This refers to your letter dated 13 June 2024, regarding your request for clarification on the following queries: 1. Is the Sangguniang Kabataan ("SK" for brevity) Chairperson entitled to the 105- days Maternity Leave? 2. Is the SK Chairperson entitled to receive honorarium while on maternity leave? 3. While on maternity leave, can the SK Chairperson continue the exercise of her functions as SK Chairperson, such as but not limited to, the signing of SK financial documents, among others? Foremost, as to the first query, we answer in the affirmative. It is well settled that SK Chairperson is one of the barangay officials entitled to leave privileges per DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2004-40 dated 05 April 2004, citing CSC-DBM Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1, series of 2004, with the subject: "Leave Benefits of Barangay Officials. Moreover, Section 4 of Republic Act No. 11210, otherwise known as the "Expanded Maternity Leave Law", as amended, provides that any pregnant female worker in the government service, regardless of employment status, in local government units, among others shall be granted a maternity leave of one hundred five (105) days with full pay regardless if the delivery was normal or ceasarian. Hence, the SK Chairperson is entitled to the 105-days Maternity Leave. As to the second query regarding entitlement to honorarium, allow us to qualify. Section 16(b) of Republic Act No. 10742, otherwise known as the "SK Reform Law of 2015", as amended, provides that the SK Chairperson shall have the same privileges enjoyed by other Sangguniang Barangay officials subject to such requirements and limitations provided under the same law. Accordingly, under the LGC, honorarium is one of the privileges of the barangay officials. Correspondingly, DILG Legal Opinion No. 28, series of 2017, citing DILG Legal Opinion No. 16, series of 2017, is instructive regarding this matter, viz: "It bears to note that under DBM Local Budget Circular No. 63, in relation to Section 393 of the Local Government Code, Sangguniang Barangay Members are paid in the form of honorarium. Corollary "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

thereto, the Govemment Accounting and Auditing Manual defines honorarium as the remuneration given to a public official for services actually rendered. Hence the grant of honorarium is based principally on services actually rendered by the claimant thereof. Accordingly, other than certain factors, the most convenient way of measuring the services actually rendered by a Sangguniang Barangay Member is attendance in sessions. Under the Local Govemment Code, Sangguniang Barangays are mandated to conduct two sessions a month. The honorarium can, therefore, be divided into two parts, each representing each session. Hence, if a Sangguniang Barangay Member will absent himself from sessions, he is not entitled to receive the proportionate amount of honorarium for services actually rendered. If he will be absent in both sessions for one month, then he can be deprived of his total honorarium for that month" Further, by definition under the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual (GAAM), honorarium is a remuneration given to a public official for services actually rendered, to be entitled to an honorarium. Thus, considering that the SK Chairperson will be on maternity leave, and would not be able to render actual service, such as attendance in sessions, we are of the considered view that she is not entitled to receive honorarium. As to the last query, we deem it prudent to qualify by stressing the purpose of the maternity leave. Under the Expanded Maternity Leave Law, one of its objectives is to protect women in the workforce and foster development of their children by giving new mothers adequate time to give birth, recover, care for, and bond with their new baby before returning to work. Accordingly, while the SK Chairperson, who is on maternity leave, may voluntarily exercise of her functions as SK Chairperson, such as but not limited to, the signing of SK financial documents, however, we are of the opinion that to allow her to do so, would defeat the very purpose of the law. In other words, it is our humble opinion that such arrangement would be a circumvention of the intent and purpose of the law on maternity leave. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, THEA T RITY OF THES CRETARY: AN VICTOR R. LLAMAS ecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLDtrjki Page 2 of 2
